Hot Wheels Goes After LEGO with Its Own Formula 1 Car Collections
31 photos
Photo: Hot Wheels
At the end of last week, Danish toymaker LEGO announced it is releasing minifigures of all this season's Formula 1 drivers, accompanied by all 11 cars that were on the grid of F1 races these past few months. It didn't take long for competitor Hot Wheels to reply.
The Mattel-owned brand already had such a collection of 1:64-scale cars in its portfolio, but it was, until now, incomplete. That changes from early next year, when the representations of newcomers Cadillac Formula 1 and Audi Revolut F1 will join the party for the first time.
Their arrival marks the completion of the collection, with all 11 teams now represented, each with two cars (unlike LEGO , which offers a single car per team). The refreshed range will become available at retailers in a gradual manner, starting early next year.
The first to land will be Sergio Perez’s No. 11 Cadillac and Gabriel Bortoleto’s No. 5 Audi Revolut, which will hit shelves in February 2027. Valtteri Bottas’ No. 77 and Nico Hulkenberg’s No. 27 will make their entrance later in the year.
Technically speaking, these new toys are nowhere near what LEGO has to offer, in terms of everything from complexity to size. These are small die-casts, unlike the DIY plastic cars the Danes throw on the market, and are priced as such: $9.99 each (LEGO's cost $29.99).
For that cash, collectors get access to replicas of the race cars wearing their updated liveries, but also the technical and visual modifications that were enforced this year: new front and rear wing geometry and updated overall proportions.
Each of the cars, sold as part of the Hot Wheels Premium Formula 1 collection, comes with a metal body and chassis, wheels shod in Real Riders tires, and a display plinth so that they can be properly shown off.
Those wishing to get their hands on the complete collection can opt for the Hot Wheels Formula 1 Season Display Set, which, at $220, throws in all 22 cars, but also a double-sided display mat so that they can be properly lined up. This collection becomes available next week, on December 4.
Aside from the cars mentioned above, there are a couple of side dishes related to F1 that can be had as well. Track sets selling from $28.99 to $149.99 allow people, among other things, to recreate races in either head-to-head or side-by-side modes, but only from the spring of 2027, when they arrive in stores.
Finally, a Silver Series Tooned Formula 1 set takes all the 11 cars from the 2026 season and morphs them into things with exaggerated proportions and unique styling. Each of them, also in 1:64 scale, sells for $3.99 and comes complete with authentic team logos and sponsorship details, front and rear wing decorations, and team-specific driver helmet colors.
There is no fixed release date for these things, as they'll become available throughout the year.
